releases.summary: NoxTLS 0.3.15 cuts RAM use on embedded targets several-fold without dropping features: a TLS 1.3 client needs about 33 KB of heap during the handshake and 17 KB once connected (4.7 KB with 4 KB records), down from about 102 KB and 71 KB, and the unified connection object shrinks from 25.5 KB to 2.8 KB. The release also makes the CTR_DRBG conform to NIST SP 800-90A, makes ML-KEM, ML-DSA, Falcon and SLH-DSA conform to their standards, adds working LMS/HSS and XMSS/XMSS^MT stateful hash-based signatures, replaces the TLS 1.2 handshake buffer with running hashes, hardens the TLS 1.2 defaults (forward-secret AEAD suites only, no SHA-1 signatures), and adds a PSK-only TLS 1.3 build option. Applications must be rebuilt: public structure layouts changed.
highlights: TLS 1.3 client heap: about 102 KB to 33 KB during the handshake and 71 KB to 17 KB once connected; worst-case stack 17.5 KB to 6.3 KB on Cortex-M4.
x509_certificate_t is a zero-copy view of the DER (8,216 B to 152 B); P-256 verify needs about 2 KB of heap instead of 20 KB.
CTR_DRBG conforms to NIST SP 800-90A Rev.1 and passes all 4,320 AES CTR_DRBG vectors of the NIST CAVP files (72 are checked in and run on every build; the full set runs from the CAVP .rsp files).

ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), Falcon and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) pass official vectors; LMS/HSS (RFC 8554) and XMSS/XMSS^MT (RFC 8391) are implemented with fail-closed stateful signing; all run on Cortex-M4 in at most about 4 KB of stack.
New PSK-only TLS 1.3 option (NOXTLS_TLS13_PEER_CERTIFICATES=0) saves about 25 KB of flash in a TLS 1.3 image.
TLS 1.2 is hardened by default: forward-secret AEAD suites only and no SHA-1 signatures; legacy suites and SHA-1 are explicit opt-ins.
changes: Large RAM reduction for embedded TLS: a TLS 1.3 client's steady-state heap falls from about 71 KB to about 17 KB (about 4.7 KB with 4 KB records), the handshake heap peak from about 102 KB to about 33 KB, and the unified connection object from 25.5 KB to 2.8 KB on Cortex-M4.

TLS records are encrypted and decrypted in place with one lazily allocated, suite-sized transmit buffer; handshake-only state (key shares, ECDHE/FFDHE secrets, ML-KEM keys, handshake workspace, transcript) is freed and wiped when the connection reaches CONNECTED, and TLS 1.3 uses a running transcript hash.
noxtls_tls_connection_t holds the TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 contexts in a union (conn->ver.tls12 / conn->ver.tls13); DTLS-only state is compiled out when DTLS is off.

New role switches NOXTLS_FEATURE_TLS_CLIENT and NOXTLS_FEATURE_TLS_SERVER compile out the unused role; server session and ticket caches are sized by NOXTLS_TLS12_SESSION_CACHE_SIZE, NOXTLS_TLS12_TICKET_CACHE_SIZE, NOXTLS_TLS12_TICKET_MAX_LEN and NOXTLS_TLS13_PSK_TICKET_STORE_MAX and store SNI/ALPN as digests.

x509_certificate_t is a zero-copy view of the certificate DER (8,216 B to 152 B on Cortex-M4); new accessors, a SAN iterator, borrow-mode parsing, lazily grown chains, borrowed/moved/DER-backed trust stores, and in-place CRL lookup. Peer certificates are released after the handshake unless NOXTLS_TLS_RETAIN_PEER_CERT=1.
Certificate and CSR writers encode directly into the output buffer; output is byte-identical for the same inputs.

noxtls_sha_ctx_t is a tagged union of per-algorithm states (944 B to 216 B, 108 B in the minimal client profile); HMAC keeps precomputed key-pad states inline and never allocates; HKDF, PBKDF2 and the TLS PRFs key HMAC once and stream their inputs.

AES T-tables, Ed25519 base tables, the RSA prime wheel and ARIA/Camellia S-boxes are constant data in flash instead of RAM tables built at runtime (about 17 KB of static RAM moved to flash). New NOXTLS_AES_ROM_TABLES, NOXTLS_AES_COMPACT_TABLES, NOXTLS_GCM_TABLE_BITS and NOXTLS_AES_CTX_RAW_KEY options.

ECC defaults to the flash P-256 generator table and low-RAM verification with the global precompute cache off; precompute tables are compact affine, curves are shared const descriptors, ECC_MAX_KEY_SIZE follows the enabled curves (NOXTLS_ECC_ENABLE_<curve>), and P-384 has dedicated field arithmetic. P-256 verify heap falls from about 20 KB to about 2 KB.
RSA uses a table-free public exponentiation, public-only keys (noxtls_rsa_key_init_public) and blinded, fault-checked CRT for private operations (RSA-2048 signing about 3.6x faster).

ML-KEM now implements FIPS 203, ML-DSA implements FIPS 204 (it was previously non-functional), Falcon key generation works and signing reproduces the NIST KAT, and SLH-DSA conforms to FIPS 205; all pass official NIST vectors, use at most about 4 KB of stack on Cortex-M, and run under QEMU on Cortex-M4/M33 (scripts/run_arm_tests.sh, .github/workflows/arm-pq.yml). noxtls_slhdsa_sign, like the ML-DSA and Falcon sign functions, now reads *signature_len as the output buffer capacity.

The AES CTR_DRBG conforms to NIST SP 800-90A Rev.1 and passes all 4,320 AES CTR_DRBG vectors of the NIST CAVP test files: Block_Cipher_df is the default (drbg_instantiate), a no-derivation-function variant and prediction resistance are available through drbg_instantiate_ex (DRBG_FLAG_NO_DF, DRBG_FLAG_PREDICTION_RESISTANCE), drbg_generate reseeds automatically after DRBG_RESEED_INTERVAL (2^48) requests and after fork on POSIX hosts, and the shared PKC DRBG reseeds every NOXTLS_PKC_RNG_RESEED_INTERVAL (1024) requests. DRBG output changes for the same inputs; drbg_state_t stays 64 bytes.

LMS/HSS (RFC 8554, NIST SP 800-208) is implemented for every parameter set (SHA-256, SHA-256/192, SHAKE256/256, SHAKE256/192; H5 to H25; W1 to W8) and HSS with up to 8 levels: stateless streaming verification with no heap and under 1.3 KB of stack on Cortex-M4, and stateful signing through noxtls_hss_key_load / noxtls_hss_sign that persists the key state through a mandatory callback before every signature, fails closed, verifies each signature before release and supports reservations and a low-RAM traversal cache. Vectors from RFC 8554 Appendix F, draft-fluhrer-lms-more-parm-sets and NIST ACVP pass. noxtls_lms_sign() now always returns NOT_SUPPORTED because a const key cannot record state; new return code NOXTLS_RETURN_KEY_EXHAUSTED.

XMSS and XMSS^MT (RFC 8391, NIST SP 800-208) are implemented for all parameter sets (SHA-256, SHA-256/192, SHAKE256/256, SHAKE256/192, RFC SHAKE128 and optional n=64): streaming verification with no heap and about 1.8 KB of stack on Cortex-M4 (3.4 KB of flash for a verify-only build), deterministic and DRBG key generation in the xmss-reference private-key format, stateful signing through noxtls_xmss_signer_* with a mandatory persistence callback that persists before release, fails closed, supports reserve-N, wipes the key on exhaustion and verifies every signature before release, and optional BDS traversal in a caller buffer. New knobs NOXTLS_XMSS_ENABLE_SHA2, NOXTLS_XMSS_ENABLE_SHAKE, NOXTLS_XMSS_ENABLE_N64, NOXTLS_XMSS_MAX_HEIGHT, NOXTLS_XMSS_ENABLE_SIGN and NOXTLS_XMSS_SIGN_SELF_CHECK. XMSS^MT parameter constants now encode the RFC 8391 OIDs (NOXTLS_XMSSMT_SHA2_20_2_256 is 0x10001), the secret key length follows the parameter set, and noxtls_xmss_sign() (const key) stays NOT_SUPPORTED.

New PSK-only TLS 1.3 / DTLS 1.3 profile: NOXTLS_TLS13_PEER_CERTIFICATES=0 (CMake NOXTLS_TLS13_PEER_CERTIFICATES=OFF) removes the peer Certificate and CertificateVerify receive paths; a client aborts with handshake_failure when the server does not select its PSK, and a server never sends CertificateRequest. On Cortex-M4 a TLS 1.3 image shrinks by about 25 KB of flash (16 KB in the minimal client profile) and its worst-case connect stack by 920 B (472 B).

TLS 1.2 no longer buffers the handshake transcript: Finished, the RFC 7627 session hash and both CertificateVerify directions are computed from running SHA-256/SHA-384 hash states (MD5+SHA-1 for TLS 1.0/1.1) that are freed at CONNECTED, so the certificate chain is no longer held for the whole handshake (handshake heap peak about 1.0 KB lower for the client, 1.2 KB for the server and 1.6 KB for a server with client authentication).

TLS 1.2 client authentication: the server CertificateRequest lists ECDSA, RSA-PSS (rsae) and RSA PKCS#1 with SHA-256/SHA-384 only, and a CertificateVerify with an unlisted scheme is rejected with illegal_parameter; the client picks its CertificateVerify scheme from the CertificateRequest. The TLS 1.2 client now offers extended_master_secret by default (noxtls_tls12_set_client_extended_master_secret) and enforces the RFC 7627 resumption rules. New digest-input APIs: noxtls_ecdsa_sign_digest, noxtls_ecdsa_verify_digest, noxtls_rsa_sign_digest, noxtls_rsa_verify_pss_digest.

Profile presets no longer override -D options; NOXTLS_PROFILE_MINIMAL_TLS_CLIENT now enables ECDSA so it can authenticate servers, limits ECC to P-256, and compiles out X448, the server role, stdio and certificate failure-detail strings.

New regression suites: TLS 1.2/1.3/unified/DTLS loopback (including allocation-failure sweeps), X.509, symmetric and public-key known-answer tests, post-quantum KATs, per-operation heap gates, a RAM budget gate and OpenSSL interoperability tests.

TLS 1.2 defaults are hardened: only forward-secret AEAD suites and SHA-256 or stronger signatures, in both directions. CBC, static-RSA and 3DES suites (NOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_LEGACY_CIPHER_SUITES) and SHA-1 signatures (new NOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_SHA1_SIGNATURES) are opt-in; TLS 1.0/1.1 keep their legacy suites for those versions only.

The bare-metal known-answer test images (post-quantum, Ed25519, AES-GCM, CMAC) now run under QEMU on Cortex-M3, M4, M7 and M33 and on RISC-V RV32IMAC and RV64IMAC (scripts/run_arm_tests.sh --cpu, QEMU virt). New toolchain files cmake/toolchains/riscv-none-elf-rv32imac.cmake and riscv-none-elf-rv64imac.cmake, and CI jobs for every target.

breaking_changes.change: x509_certificate_t is a zero-copy view of the certificate DER; fields such as subject_dn, san_dns_names, not_before and not_after were removed.
breaking_changes.migration: Use the accessor functions and the SAN iterator, and keep the DER buffer alive while a borrowed certificate is in use.

breaking_changes.change: TLS 1.3 handshake-only fields moved into a handshake block that is freed when the connection reaches CONNECTED.
breaking_changes.migration: Do not read handshake internals after CONNECTED; use the public getters.

breaking_changes.change: tls12_context_t no longer has handshake_messages or ems_session_transcript_len.
breaking_changes.migration: handshake_messages_len still reports the number of handshake bytes hashed.

breaking_changes.change: noxtls_tls_connection_t holds the TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 contexts in a union.
breaking_changes.migration: Access them as conn->ver.tls12 and conn->ver.tls13.

breaking_changes.change: drbg_state_t no longer stores seedlen and keylen; DRBG output differs from earlier versions for the same inputs; caller entropy below the SP 800-90A minimum returns NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_ENOUGH_ENTROPY.
breaking_changes.migration: Pass NULL entropy to let the DRBG draw it, and take expected test values from NIST CAVP vectors.

breaking_changes.change: ML-KEM shared secrets and SLH-DSA signatures differ from earlier versions, which were not standard-conformant.
breaking_changes.migration: Regenerate stored test vectors and do not interoperate with keys or ciphertexts produced by 0.3.14 or earlier.

breaking_changes.change: noxtls_slhdsa_sign reads *signature_len as the output buffer capacity, like the ML-DSA and Falcon sign functions.
breaking_changes.migration: Set the length to the buffer size before calling.

breaking_changes.change: noxtls_lms_sign() and noxtls_xmss_sign() (const key) return NOT_SUPPORTED; the LMS secret key grew from 128 to 168 bytes; the XMSS secret key length follows the parameter set; XMSS^MT parameter constants encode the RFC 8391 OIDs.
breaking_changes.migration: Use noxtls_hss_key_load / noxtls_hss_sign or noxtls_xmss_signer_*, and size buffers with the *_len helpers.

breaking_changes.change: The TLS 1.2 client offers extended_master_secret by default, and the server's CertificateRequest lists only ECDSA, RSA-PSS (rsae) and RSA PKCS#1 with SHA-256 or SHA-384.
breaking_changes.migration: Call noxtls_tls12_set_client_extended_master_secret(ctx, 0) to stop offering EMS; peers that sign CertificateVerify with SHA-1, SHA-512 or EdDSA are now rejected.

breaking_changes.change: Profile presets in noxtls_config.h no longer override -D options, and NOXTLS_PROFILE_MINIMAL_TLS_CLIENT now enables ECDSA, limits ECC to P-256 and compiles out X448, the server role, stdio and certificate failure strings.
breaking_changes.migration: Re-check builds that relied on a profile forcing a value.
HMAC no longer allocates; remove the option.

breaking_changes.change: TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 now offer and negotiate only forward-secret AEAD suites (ECDHE-ECDSA, ECDHE-RSA and DHE-RSA with AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-CCM) and use no SHA-1 signatures. Peers that support only CBC, static-RSA or 3DES suites, or only SHA-1 signatures, fail to connect; a TLS 1.2 client that sends no signature_algorithms extension is refused; application cipher-suite allowlists can no longer enable legacy suites.
breaking_changes.migration: Rebuild with -DNOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_LEGACY_CIPHER_SUITES=ON and/or -DNOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_SHA1_SIGNATURES=ON (or set NOXTLS_TLS12_ENABLE_LEGACY_CIPHER_SUITES / NOXTLS_TLS12_ENABLE_SHA1_SIGNATURES to 1); with both on, TLS 1.2 behaves as before. TLS 1.0/1.1 builds keep their CBC and MD5/SHA-1 behaviour for those versions only.

deprecations.replacement: None needed: HMAC keeps its key-pad states inline and never allocates.

fixed: noxtls_tls12_context_init and noxtls_tls13_context_init did not initialize every field; reused context memory could disable TLS 1.2 server session resumption.
noxtls_tls_connection_accept ignored a fixed TLS 1.2 init_version, a repeated handshake call after WANT_WRITE restarted the handshake, and a TLS 1.3 server kept only the last 0-RTT record.
One-shot CBC and streaming/one-shot CFB decryption gave wrong results from the second block when the output buffer was the input buffer.
ML-KEM, ML-DSA and Falcon sources did not compile when enabled.
The ECDSA nonce inverse and X448 were not computed in constant time.
Ephemeral (EC)DHE private keys, FFDHE secrets and the GCM H table were kept in memory longer than needed; AES round keys and HMAC/ChaCha20 key copies were not always wiped.
noxtls_rsa_decrypt_crt_only no longer prints decrypted data to the debug log; SSLKEYLOGFILE support is compiled only with NOXTLS_FEATURE_KEYLOG=1.

NOXTLS_MAX_CERT_SIZE is enforced when parsing DER, certificates with outer-length slack or trailing bytes are rejected, issuer names are compared per RFC 5280 instead of as truncated text, and EC certificates from generate_self_signed_with_extensions carry the namedCurve parameter.
DTLS reassembly memory is capped by NOXTLS_DTLS_REASSEMBLY_MAX_BYTES and uses bitmaps.
Application-local configuration headers are generated from noxtls_config.h, so applications and the library always agree on structure layouts.
The tls12_ocsp_stapling_regression test no longer frees an uninitialized RSA key.

The CTR_DRBG update and generate steps did not follow SP 800-90A (V was not incremented before each block, and part of the AES-128 seed material had no effect), caller entropy shorter than the seed length was silently replaced and additional input was truncated; entropy that is too short now returns NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_ENOUGH_ENTROPY, an all-equal entropy block is rejected and /dev/urandom reads retry short reads.
TLS wipes its throw-away DRBG states after drawing randoms, session IDs, ticket nonces, connection IDs and TLS 1.1 CBC IVs.

The TLS 1.2 client ECDSA CertificateVerify signature size now follows the key curve instead of a fixed 32 or 48 bytes; TLS 1.0/1.1 client authentication, which sent TLS 1.2-format messages, now fails explicitly; https_server --require-client-cert also requires the certificate for TLS 1.2.
X.509 parsing accepted non-minimal DER lengths and CRLs followed by trailing bytes, and a truncated distinguished-name rendering could fuse attribute values.

The TLS 1.3 HkdfLabel length check could wrap for very long labels, allowing an out-of-bounds read; the RFC 8449 record size limit did not count the inner content type; a PSK binder that did not validate did not abort the handshake; the TLS 1.3 exporter omitted the RFC 8446 Derive-Secret step, so exported keying material did not match other implementations.

TLS 1.2 CBC records used a predictable explicit IV (write_IV XOR sequence number); the client did not signal secure renegotiation (RFC 5746) or check the server's renegotiation_info; a resumption cancelled by an SNI mismatch kept the cached cipher suite and lost the ALPN result; the polled accept path sent no alert when it rejected a client CertificateVerify.

resolved.title: TLS context init left fields uninitialized
resolved.description: noxtls_tls12_context_init and noxtls_tls13_context_init did not initialize every field; reused context memory could disable TLS 1.2 server session resumption.

resolved.title: Unified accept ignored init_version; handshake re-entry restarted
resolved.description: noxtls_tls_connection_accept ignored a fixed TLS 1.2 init_version, a repeated handshake call after WANT_WRITE restarted the handshake, and a TLS 1.3 server kept only the last 0-RTT record.

resolved.title: In-place CBC/CFB decryption gave wrong output
resolved.description: One-shot CBC and streaming/one-shot CFB decryption gave wrong results from the second block when the output buffer was the input buffer.

resolved.title: ML-KEM, ML-DSA and Falcon did not compile
resolved.description: ML-KEM, ML-DSA and Falcon sources did not compile when enabled; ML-DSA was non-functional and Falcon key generation never finished.

resolved.title: ECDSA nonce inverse and X448 not constant time
resolved.description: The ECDSA nonce inversion and X448 scalar multiplication were not computed in constant time.

resolved.title: Secrets kept in memory longer than needed
resolved.description: Ephemeral (EC)DHE private keys, FFDHE secrets and the GCM H table were kept in memory longer than needed; AES round keys and HMAC/ChaCha20 key copies were not always wiped.

resolved.title: RSA CRT decryption logged plaintext; key log always built
resolved.description: noxtls_rsa_decrypt_crt_only printed decrypted data to the debug log, and SSLKEYLOGFILE support was always compiled in. It is now built only with NOXTLS_FEATURE_KEYLOG=1.

resolved.title: X.509 parsing accepted malformed input
resolved.description: NOXTLS_MAX_CERT_SIZE was not enforced when parsing DER, certificates with outer-length slack or trailing bytes were accepted, issuer names were compared as truncated text instead of per RFC 5280, and EC certificates from generate_self_signed_with_extensions lacked the namedCurve parameter.

resolved.title: DTLS reassembly memory unbounded
resolved.description: DTLS reassembly memory is now capped by NOXTLS_DTLS_REASSEMBLY_MAX_BYTES and uses bitmaps.

resolved.title: Application configs drifted from the library config
resolved.description: Application-local configuration headers are generated from noxtls_config.h, so applications and the library always agree on structure layouts.

resolved.title: OCSP stapling regression test freed an uninitialized key
resolved.description: The tls12_ocsp_stapling_regression test no longer frees an uninitialized RSA key.

resolved.title: CTR_DRBG did not conform to SP 800-90A
resolved.description: V was not incremented before each block, part of the AES-128 seed material had no effect, caller entropy shorter than the seed length was silently replaced and additional input was truncated. Entropy that is too short now returns NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_ENOUGH_ENTROPY, an all-equal entropy block is rejected and /dev/urandom reads retry short reads.

resolved.title: TLS left temporary DRBG states on the stack
resolved.description: TLS now wipes its throw-away DRBG states after drawing randoms, session IDs, ticket nonces, connection IDs and TLS 1.1 CBC IVs.

resolved.title: TLS 1.2 client authentication defects
resolved.description: The TLS 1.2 client ECDSA CertificateVerify signature size was fixed at 32 or 48 bytes instead of following the key curve; TLS 1.0/1.1 client authentication sent TLS 1.2-format messages and now fails explicitly; https_server --require-client-cert did not require the certificate for TLS 1.2.

resolved.title: X.509 accepted non-minimal DER lengths; truncated DN text fused values
resolved.description: asn1_get_length accepted long-form lengths that are not minimal, so one signed certificate had several valid encodings (different hashes, pins and channel bindings). A truncated distinguished-name rendering could skip a separator but still append the value.

resolved.title: CRL with trailing bytes was accepted
resolved.description: A CRL whose CertificateList was followed by extra bytes parsed successfully; it is now rejected, as for certificates.

resolved.title: HkdfLabel length check could wrap
resolved.description: hkdf_expand_label checked prefix_len + label_len after adding them, so a very long label could wrap the sum and cause an out-of-bounds read.

resolved.title: RFC 8449 record size limit off by one
resolved.description: The TLS 1.3 record_size_limit did not count the inner content type byte.

resolved.title: Invalid PSK binder did not abort the handshake
resolved.description: RFC 8446 4.2.11 requires the server to abort when the selected PSK's binder does not validate; the server skipped the identity and completed a full certificate handshake instead. It now sends decrypt_error.

resolved.title: SNI mismatch on resumption kept the cached suite
resolved.description: When the ClientHello server_name did not match the cached session, the cancelled resumption left the cached session's cipher suite selected (possibly outside the server allowlist) and cleared the negotiated ALPN.

resolved.title: No alert when the polled accept path rejected CertificateVerify
resolved.description: The TLS 1.2 polled accept path closed without sending an alert after rejecting a client CertificateVerify.

resolved.title: TLS 1.3 exporter did not match RFC 8446
resolved.description: noxtls_tls13_export_keying_material omitted the Derive-Secret step of RFC 8446 7.5, so its output did not match other TLS 1.3 implementations (EAP-TLS, channel bindings).

resolved.title: Predictable explicit CBC IV in TLS 1.2
resolved.description: TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 CBC records used write_IV XOR sequence number as the explicit IV, which an attacker can predict (RFC 5246 6.2.3.2). The IV now comes from the DRBG.

resolved.title: Secure renegotiation not signalled
resolved.description: The TLS 1.2 client sent neither the empty renegotiation_info extension nor TLS_EMPTY_RENEGOTIATION_INFO_SCSV on the initial ClientHello (RFC 5746 3.4) and did not check the server's renegotiation_info.

resolved.title: TLS 1.2 offered and accepted SHA-1 signatures by default
resolved.description: The TLS 1.2 client offered rsa_pkcs1_sha1 and ecdsa_sha1, and the server signed ServerKeyExchange with SHA-1 when the client listed it or sent no signature_algorithms extension. SHA-1 signatures are now neither offered nor accepted by default (resolves NOXTLS-KA-0.3.15-12).

resolved.title: TLS 1.2 offered CBC, static-RSA and 3DES suites by default
resolved.description: The TLS 1.2 default offer included AES-CBC suites, static-RSA key exchange and DHE_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA, contrary to BUILDING.md. TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 now offer and negotiate only forward-secret AEAD suites by default (resolves NOXTLS-KA-0.3.15-13).

resolved.title: TLS 1.2 client accepted an unoffered suite or signature scheme
resolved.description: The client failed without an alert when the ServerHello chose a suite it had not offered, and after a TLS 1.3 to 1.2 downgrade it checked the suite and ServerKeyExchange scheme against its TLS 1.2 table rather than the ClientHello it actually sent. It now checks both against the sent ClientHello and sends illegal_parameter.

known_issues: Public structure layouts changed (TLS contexts, x509_certificate_t, CRL, hash/HMAC/AES/ChaCha/ARIA/DRBG contexts, ECC curve parameters); applications must be rebuilt against the new headers.
ML-KEM shared secrets, SLH-DSA signatures and DRBG output differ from earlier NoxTLS versions because those were not standard-conformant.
The library does not implement SP 800-90B noise-source health tests; ports that supply a raw TRNG through the entropy callback must provide them.

LMS/HSS and XMSS private keys are stateful: restoring an older copy of a key (backup, cloned flash, VM snapshot) reuses one-time keys. Keep a single, monotonically updated copy and persist through the signer callback.

anomalies.title: No SP 800-90B entropy health tests
anomalies.description: The library does not implement SP 800-90B noise-source health tests (repetition count, adaptive proportion, start-up tests). It only rejects an entropy block whose bytes are all equal.
anomalies.workaround: Ports that feed a raw hardware RNG through the entropy callback must run the health tests themselves, or use an OS CSPRNG or an SP 800-90B validated conditioned source.

anomalies.title: Restoring an old LMS/HSS or XMSS private key reuses one-time keys
anomalies.description: LMS/HSS and XMSS keys are stateful. Restoring an older copy of the key state (backup, cloned flash, VM snapshot) causes one-time keys to be reused, which can allow forgeries. LMS detects this only when a newer traversal workspace is reused; XMSS cannot detect it.
anomalies.workaround: Keep exactly one, monotonically updated copy of each key, persist it through the signer callback with A/B slots and a checksum, and never restore it from backups.

anomalies.title: XMSS exhaustion: result of the final key write is ignored
anomalies.description: When an XMSS key signs with its last index, the library persists an image with the seeds wiped but ignores whether that write succeeds. No index can be reused, because the stored index is already at the end marker, but a failed write leaves the seeds in the stored copy.
anomalies.workaround: Have the persistence callback verify each write, and erase an exhausted key's storage explicitly.

anomalies.title: LMS and XMSS return different codes for the same errors
anomalies.description: A signature buffer that is too small returns INVALID_PARAM from LMS and INVALID_BLOCK_SIZE from XMSS; a wrong signature length at verification returns FAILED from LMS and BAD_DATA from XMSS.
anomalies.workaround: Treat any non-SUCCESS result as failure.

anomalies.title: TLS 1.2 renegotiation transcript reset not verified end to end
anomalies.description: Server-initiated renegotiation from OpenSSL s_client already failed before this release, so the reset of the TLS 1.2 running transcript on renegotiation is covered by code review and the secure-renegotiation test only.
anomalies.workaround: Keep renegotiation disabled; the NoxTLS client declines it.

anomalies.title: Hash accelerator ports not tested with interleaved transcript states
anomalies.description: TLS 1.2 now copies and interleaves several hash states during the handshake, as TLS 1.3 already did. This is safe for software hashing and for ports that keep state in the context, but hardware hash ports were not tested.
anomalies.workaround: Run the TLS loopback suite on the target when a hardware hash backend is enabled.

anomalies.title: EC-JPAKE static DRBG has no periodic reseed
anomalies.description: The EC-JPAKE module keeps a static DRBG instance that reseeds only at the SP 800-90A interval limit, not periodically. It does reseed after fork on POSIX hosts.
anomalies.workaround: None needed for typical use; EC-JPAKE is off by default.

anomalies.title: DRBG fork detection not exercised on a POSIX host
anomalies.description: Fork detection (reseed in a forked child) compiles on POSIX targets but was not run on a POSIX host during verification.
anomalies.workaround: Reseed or re-instantiate DRBG instances explicitly after fork.

anomalies.title: MISRA C:2025 findings open
anomalies.description: The CodeNox scan of this release reports 28 Mandatory findings (all inconclusive, under review), 940 Required and 3,177 Advisory findings (CodeNox 0.2.1). See the MISRA analysis report.
anomalies.workaround: Projects with MISRA obligations should review the report and the analyst notes for the modules they use.

anomalies.title: XMSS traversal state is RAM-only; some large parameter sets lack vectors
anomalies.description: The XMSS BDS traversal state is rebuilt on attach at about the cost of one key generation, which is impractical on an MCU for subtrees of height 20. XMSS h=20, XMSS^MT 40/2 and 60/3 and LMS H25 have no known-answer vectors and are covered by shared code paths and negative tests.
anomalies.workaround: Use XMSS^MT with subtree height 5 or 10, or XMSS h=10, on MCUs; generate large trees off-device.

anomalies.title: PSK-only build fails the certificate-based TLS 1.3 tests
anomalies.description: With NOXTLS_TLS13_PEER_CERTIFICATES=0 the existing certificate-based TLS 1.3 loopback tests fail because that path is compiled out on purpose; they are not yet skipped in that configuration.
anomalies.workaround: Run the PSK, DTLS 1.3 recovery and TLS 1.2 tests for PSK-only builds.

anomalies.title: constant_time_strict side-channel profile has no extra effect
anomalies.description: NOXTLS_SIDECHANNEL_PROFILE_CONSTANT_TIME_STRICT behaves like the balanced profile: both enable constant-time secret comparison, but the additional strict hardening described in BUILDING.md is not implemented.
anomalies.workaround: None; balanced and strict give the same protection. Do not rely on strict for additional guarantees.

anomalies.title: Default configuration enables legacy algorithms
anomalies.description: The default noxtls_config.h enables MD5, SHA-1, RC4, DES/3DES and DSA (the minimal and FIPS-like profiles disable them).
anomalies.workaround: Disable unused legacy algorithms (NOXTLS_FEATURE_RC4=0, NOXTLS_FEATURE_DES=0, NOXTLS_FEATURE_DSA=0, NOXTLS_FEATURE_MD5=0 where not needed) or start from a profile.

anomalies.title: Encrypt-then-MAC not negotiated for three legacy CBC suites
anomalies.description: TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA, TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA and TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA are missing from the Encrypt-then-MAC (RFC 7366) suite list, so they use MAC-then-encrypt even when both peers offer EtM. Only builds with NOXTLS_TLS12_ENABLE_LEGACY_CIPHER_SUITES=1 are affected.
anomalies.workaround: Keep the legacy suites off (the default), or prefer the other CBC suites.

anomalies.title: TLS 1.3 CertificateRequest lists SHA-1 signature schemes
anomalies.description: The TLS 1.3 server CertificateRequest signature_algorithms list still includes rsa_pkcs1_sha1 (0x0201) and ecdsa_sha1 (0x0203), and SHA-224 schemes. RFC 8446 does not allow SHA-1 in CertificateVerify.
anomalies.workaround: None needed for clients that sign CertificateVerify with SHA-256 or stronger, which all current TLS 1.3 implementations do.

security.title: Timing side channels in ECDSA signing and X448
security.description: The ECDSA nonce inversion and X448 scalar multiplication were not constant time, which can leak information about the nonce or private key to an attacker who can measure timing precisely. Fixed: the nonce inversion is blinded and X448 uses constant-time field arithmetic.

security.title: CTR_DRBG did not conform to SP 800-90A
security.description: The DRBG update and generate steps deviated from SP 800-90A, part of the AES-128 seed material had no effect, and caller entropy that was too short was silently replaced. No practical attack is known, but the generator did not meet its stated standard. Fixed and validated against all NIST CAVP vectors.

security.title: Decrypted data written to the debug log
security.description: noxtls_rsa_decrypt_crt_only printed decrypted data, and private primes were logged on some paths, when debug logging was enabled. Fixed: these values are no longer logged.
security.affected_versions: 0.3.14 and earlier, builds with debug logging enabled

security.title: X.509 parser accepted malformed certificates
security.description: Certificates with outer-length slack or trailing bytes were accepted, NOXTLS_MAX_CERT_SIZE was not enforced during DER parsing, and issuer names were compared as truncated text. Fixed: such input is rejected and names are compared per RFC 5280.

security.title: Secrets and key material retained in memory
security.description: Ephemeral (EC)DHE private keys, FFDHE secrets, AES round keys, HMAC and ChaCha20 key copies, throw-away DRBG states and the GCM H table were kept or left unwiped longer than needed. Fixed: they are wiped and freed as soon as they are no longer needed.

security.title: TLS key logging compiled in by default
security.description: SSLKEYLOGFILE support, which writes TLS secrets to a file, was compiled into every build. It is now built only with NOXTLS_FEATURE_KEYLOG=1.

security.title: DTLS reassembly memory not bounded
security.description: A peer could make DTLS handshake reassembly use more memory than intended. Reassembly is now capped by NOXTLS_DTLS_REASSEMBLY_MAX_BYTES.

security.title: TLS 1.2 server offered unverified CertificateVerify schemes
security.description: The TLS 1.2 server's CertificateRequest listed SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-512, EdDSA and rsa_pss_pss schemes it never verified. It now lists only the schemes it verifies and rejects others with illegal_parameter.

security.title: Predictable explicit IV in TLS 1.2 CBC records
security.description: TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 CBC-mode records used write_IV XOR sequence number as the explicit IV. An attacker who can inject chosen plaintext could predict the IV (BEAST-style). Fixed: the IV is drawn from the DRBG. CBC suites are also no longer enabled by default.

security.title: Out-of-bounds read in the TLS 1.3 HkdfLabel construction
security.description: A label length close to the 32-bit limit could wrap the HkdfLabel length check and cause an out-of-bounds read, for example through an application-supplied exporter label. Fixed: the label length is bounded before the prefix is added.

security.title: Secure renegotiation (RFC 5746) not signalled by the TLS 1.2 client
security.description: The client did not signal or verify secure renegotiation. The NoxTLS client declines renegotiation, which limits the impact. Fixed: the SCSV is sent and the server's renegotiation_info is checked.

security.title: TLS 1.3 server continued after an invalid PSK binder
security.description: A ClientHello with a PSK binder that did not validate was handled as a full certificate handshake instead of being rejected as RFC 8446 requires. The PSK was not accepted, so this did not bypass authentication. Fixed: the server aborts with decrypt_error.

security.title: TLS 1.2 resumption fallback could select a suite outside the server allowlist
security.description: When an SNI mismatch cancelled a resumption, the server kept the cached session's cipher suite for the full handshake. Fixed: the suite is selected again from the ClientHello and the allowlist.

security.title: Non-canonical DER accepted in X.509 parsing
security.description: Non-minimal DER length encodings and CRLs with trailing bytes were accepted, so one certificate or CRL could have several valid encodings, which affects hash-based pinning and channel bindings. Fixed: they are rejected.

security.title: TLS 1.2 defaults allowed SHA-1 signatures and non-forward-secret or CBC suites
security.description: By default the TLS 1.2 client offered SHA-1 signature schemes (deprecated by RFC 9155) and CBC, static-RSA and 3DES suites, and the server negotiated them. The client also accepted a ServerHello suite or ServerKeyExchange scheme it had not offered after a TLS 1.3 to 1.2 downgrade. Fixed: only forward-secret AEAD suites and SHA-256 or stronger signatures by default; legacy behaviour needs NOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_LEGACY_CIPHER_SUITES and NOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_SHA1_SIGNATURES.

security_recommendations: Supply a full-entropy source: an OS CSPRNG, an SP 800-90B validated conditioned source, or a raw TRNG that your port conditions and health-tests. Never ship NOXTLS_ENTROPY_SOURCE_DUMMY.

Keep TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 off, and leave NOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_LEGACY_CIPHER_SUITES and NOXTLS_CFG_TLS12_ENABLE_SHA1_SIGNATURES at their default (off) unless an interoperability requirement forces them. Disable RC4, DES, MD4 and MD5-based options where not needed.
Leave NOXTLS_FEATURE_KEYLOG off in production builds; key logs expose all session secrets.
Keep the TLS 1.2 extended_master_secret offer enabled (the default) and prefer TLS 1.3.
Enable certificate validity checking (NOXTLS_HAVE_TIME=1 with a trusted clock) and hostname verification for every client connection.
For LMS/HSS and XMSS signing keys, keep one monotonically updated copy, persist it with A/B slots and a checksum through the signer callback, and never restore it from a backup or snapshot.
Use the PSK-only TLS 1.3 option (NOXTLS_TLS13_PEER_CERTIFICATES=0) only when every TLS 1.3 peer authenticates with an external PSK of at least 128 bits of entropy.
Rebuild applications against the 0.3.15 headers; public structure layouts changed and mixing headers and libraries from different versions is unsafe.

changes: The cert utility can verify that a parsed RSA, ECC, EdDSA, or enabled post-quantum private key matches the public key in an X.509 certificate using NoxTLS.
certgen genec warns when importing a caller-supplied EC scalar, showing its bit length and cautioning that small or predictable values can be brute-forced.
ECC keys can now be imported from a big-endian private scalar through noxtls_ecc_key_import_private() or certgen genec -scalar; the library validates the scalar and derives the matching public key.

fixed: Fix MSVC C test registration and compiler-specific preprocessing in the read-only Ed25519 regression suite.
known_issues: Physical hardware timing and firmware-update qualification remain pending.

changes: Optional read-only compact Ed25519 base tables eliminate 4,488 bytes of static RAM in the measured Cortex-M33 profile. NOXTLS_ED25519_READONLY_SMALL_BASE defaults to OFF; enabling it selects the existing compact-base algorithm.
Tables are generated from the in-house implementation and checked byte-for-byte. Default comb and lazy compact paths remain unchanged; all callers must use the same configuration.
fixed: Unsupported compact-table geometry is rejected at compile time rather than using a mismatched table.
known_issues: The change has host vector/differential and Cortex-M33 compilation/resource validation. Physical hardware timing and firmware-update qualification are separate application gates.

changes: certgen req -new creates ECC PKCS#10 certificate requests in PEM or DER format, with the public key derived from the private key.
fixed: EC certificate requests include namedCurve parameters and the mandatory attributes field.
known_issues: The certgen CSR command currently supports ECC keys and a common-name subject only. Other key types, requested extensions and AWS enrollment are not implemented by that command.

changes: Patch release on top of 0.3.7 for native library section granularity. GNU and Clang C/C++ builds use private function/data section flags on supported platforms; applications control final linker garbage collection.
No API, ABI, protocol or optimization-level changes. Apple and MSVC-compatible builds keep their existing compiler options.
fixed: Certificate, utility, SHA-3, PAKE and optional nRF54 libraries now receive section flags alongside the core libraries. Direct subdirectory builds no longer depend on the root target list.
known_issues: Earlier release limitations still apply. Applications must enable linker garbage collection to discard unused sections.

changes: Patch release on top of 0.3.6 combining shared Zephyr integration, cooperative crypto service hooks and embedded DTLS/DFU support. Rebuild the library and callers together with the same configuration.
Zephyr consumers share one NoxTLS configuration and CPU ABI across archives. Kernel monotonic time is used without a Newlib _times shim.

Software P-256 arithmetic calls the cooperative ECC service hook between bounded operations, including field inversion. The default hook does nothing; ports can provide their task-aware implementation.
NoxV CCM acceleration is opt-in and checks engine ownership, input limits and completion. Platforms can use NoxV AES/SHA without enabling P-256 acceleration.
Embedded profiles can select the TLS 1.3 ticket-store capacity. Optional CC13xx SHA-512 block callbacks support SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 under the existing AES/SHA guard.
fixed: DTLS 1.3 discards duplicate or stale records without failing the connection or delivering their plaintext. Fresh records following a duplicate in the same datagram are preserved; duplicate-discard loops remain bounded.
Zephyr and ESP-IDF configuration generation handles initializer lists and enum constants without exposing them as scalar Kconfig settings.
Mocked NoxV ECC, SHA-256 and CCM regression tests use explicit test I/O bindings and consistent accelerator profiles on GCC and MSVC.
known_issues: Earlier release limitations still apply except where explicitly fixed above. DTLS 1.2 EC-JPAKE interoperability remains unqualified.
The combined revision passes local crypto/DTLS tests, shared and secure-feature Zephyr QEMU tests, and CC1354/CC35x1 application builds. Hardware was not reflashed for this consolidation.

changes: Patch update to 0.3.5 for DTLS 1.3 recovery, embedded memory use and optional CC13xx accelerator bindings. Rebuild the library and callers together: the DTLS context gains one callback pointer for encrypted-flight retransmission.

Optional CC13xx CCM, SHA-224/256 and X25519 callbacks complement AES/GCM/P-256. AES and PKA engines bind independently, with software fallback for unbound or busy engines before admission. No vendor SDK driver dependency or new fixed record buffer is added.
fixed: DTLS 1.3 clients aborted when an encrypted handshake record arrived before final ServerHello. Undecryptable pre-key records are now discarded without acknowledging them or changing replay state, allowing retransmission to recover. Existing trailing-record handling and the bounded receive loop are preserved.

DTLS 1.3 encrypted handshake flights were not retained for retransmission. Lost server records, client Finished or final ACK could leave a half-open session and cause Secure CoAP timeouts. Flights now retransmit with fresh record sequence numbers; verified client Finished releases the completed server flight.
The TLS 1.3 key-share parser allocated 512 descriptors for a single X25519 share. It now validates the vector and allocates only the actual entry count.

Classical-only ClientHello staging used large post-quantum-sized stack arrays, causing a measured embedded task stack overflow. Classical builds now use bounded 160-byte staging; ML-KEM builds retain their existing capacities.
TLS-only builds with DTLS disabled now retain the compile guards needed by the recovery code.
known_issues: Earlier release limitations still apply except where explicitly fixed above. DTLS 1.2 EC-JPAKE interoperability remains unqualified.
Recovery is covered by native loss/reordering tests and bounded CC1354/CC35x1 Secure CoAP hardware runs. These tests do not qualify every cipher suite or long-duration operation.

changes: Patch release on top of 0.3.4 that adds two opt-in features; builds that do not enable them keep their behavior, configuration defaults and wire format.

**EC-JPAKE** (`NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_ECJPAKE`, default OFF): EC J-PAKE over P-256 (RFC 8236 section 3) with SHA-256 Schnorr NIZK proofs (RFC 8235 section 3) in the TLS form of draft-cragie-tls-ecjpake-01. API in `noxtls-lib/pake/noxtls_ecjpake.h`.

**DTLS 1.2 EC-JPAKE suite** (`NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_DTLS_ECJPAKE`, default OFF): `TLS_ECJPAKE_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8` (0xC0FF) with the `ecjpake_key_kp_pair` extension (256), the EC-JPAKE ServerKeyExchange / ClientKeyExchange and AES-128-CCM-8 records, as used by Thread MeshCoP commissioning. New API: `noxtls_tls12_set_ecjpake_password()`, `noxtls_tls12_ecjpake_negotiated()`, `noxtls_tls12_ecjpake_export_key_block()`. `noxtls_tls12_connect_poll()` / `noxtls_tls12_accept_poll()` also drive DTLS 1.2 for EC-JPAKE contexts.
Zephyr and ESP-IDF Kconfig expose both switches.
known_issues: The known issues listed for 0.3.0 still apply.
No public known-answer vectors exist for the complete EC-JPAKE TLS exchange; interoperability with other Thread implementations has not yet been tested on hardware.

changes: Patch release on top of 0.3.3. Build fix only; no API, ABI, configuration, or wire-format changes, and no change to generated code. 0.3.4 is a drop-in replacement for 0.3.3.
fixed: **Cortex-M7 and STM32 accelerated builds failed with `'NULL' undeclared`.** `noxtls_sha256_cortexm7.c`, `noxtls_stm32_hash_core.c` and `noxtls_aes_accel_stm32_port.c` used `NULL` and `size_t` without including `<stddef.h>`. They used to get the definitions indirectly through `<stdio.h>` in other NoxTLS headers, which the 0.3.0 MISRA cleanup removed, so every build that compiles the Cortex-M7 SHA-256 core or the STM32 hash/AES ports failed (for example STM32F767 and STM32H7 targets). Each file now includes `<stddef.h>` itself.
known_issues: The known issues listed for 0.3.0 still apply.

changes: Patch release on top of 0.3.2. CC13xx hardware-acceleration changes only; no API signature, ABI, or wire-format changes. Builds that do not enable a CC13xx accelerator port are unaffected.

**Per-engine CC13xx accelerator switches.** `NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_CC13XX_AES_ACCEL` and `NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_CC13XX_P256_ACCEL` select the AES and P-256 callback ports separately. `NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_CC13XX_HW_ACCEL` remains an umbrella that enables both, so existing configurations behave as before. See [CC13xx hardware accelerator](./cc13xx-accelerator.md).
**New `noxtls_cc13xx_aes_blocks()`.** Runs a batch of AES blocks while holding the AES engine, used by the CTR DRBG.

**Behavior change for direct binding callers.** A request that finds its engine busy now returns `NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_SUPPORTED` (fall back to software) instead of `NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_INITIALIZED`. Callers that use the AES and ECC APIs are unaffected. See [Upgrading from 0.3.2](./cc13xx-accelerator.md#upgrading-from-032).
fixed: **CC13xx AES failed during a P-256 multiply.** The AES engine and the PKA shared one busy flag, and the busy check ran before the missing-callback fallback, so an AES block requested while a yielding P-256 multiply was in progress failed with `NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_INITIALIZED` instead of falling back to software, even when no AES callback was bound. Each engine now has its own guard, and a busy or unbound engine falls back to software. Severity: Medium (availability); not a memory-safety issue.
**CC13xx busy flag race.** The guard was a plain flag checked and then set, so two tasks or a task and an interrupt could both enter the binding. The per-engine guards now use atomic test-and-set.
**CTR DRBG batch interrupted between blocks.** Another task could take the AES engine between blocks of a DRBG batch and fail it partway. The batch now holds the engine for its duration.
known_issues: The known issues listed for 0.3.0 still apply.

changes: Patch release on top of 0.3.0. No API, ABI, configuration, or wire-format changes; 0.3.2 is a drop-in replacement for 0.3.0. For the MISRA C:2025 conversion, the security fixes, and upgrade notes from 0.2.x, read the 0.3.0 release notes (select **0.3.0** in the version dropdown) and [Security fixes in 0.3.0](./security-fixes-0.3.0.md).
fixed: **TLS 1.3 handshake records that continue a message.** RFC 8446 section 5.1 allows a handshake message to span records, but the record layer read the first byte of every decrypted handshake record as a message type. When a peer split a message such as Certificate or Finished and the continuation record started with 0x18 (KeyUpdate), the handshake was aborted with unexpected_message; with 0x05 (EndOfEarlyData) a client aborted and a server recorded EndOfEarlyData too early, which could end the 0-RTT phase. The failure depended on certificate or Finished bytes, so it appeared as an intermittent handshake failure of about 1 in 128 for each affected split. The KeyUpdate and EndOfEarlyData checks now apply only to records that start a new handshake message. DTLS is not affected. Severity: Medium (handshake availability); not a memory-safety issue.
known_issues: The known issues listed for 0.3.0 still apply, except the TLS 1.3 fragmented-handshake issue fixed in this release.

changes: **MISRA C:2025.** NoxTLS 0.3.0 is the first release built against MISRA C:2025. Mandatory and Required findings were fixed in the code, with no suppressions or blanket exemptions. Every recorded library scan shows 0 Mandatory findings. The latest recorded integration scan (96 translation units) lists 24 Required findings with draft technical dispositions awaiting project sign-off. Advisory findings are not claimed, and NoxTLS is not certified under any functional-safety standard. See [MISRA C:2025](./misra-c.md).

**Security fixes.** 0.3.0 fixes 26 security issues: two rated Critical, fourteen rated High, seven rated Medium, and three rated Low. Fourteen of them (four High, seven Medium, and three Low) were found by a final round of fuzz testing, code review, and interoperability testing. Each one is described in [Security fixes in 0.3.0](./security-fixes-0.3.0.md), including the affected APIs and configurations, what an attacker could do, what changed, and whether you need to act. No CVE identifiers have been assigned. In summary:
  - **Critical:** RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepted forged signatures (practical against RSA keys with public exponent 3). Affects X.509 certificate verification and TLS 1.2 signature checks. Present in 0.2.x.
  - **Critical:** X.509 chain verification accepted a CA certificate that copied a trust anchor's subject and serial number, so certificates issued under an attacker's key could be trusted.
  - **High:** `noxtls_parse_der()` accepted malformed DER in non-debug builds. Introduced during 0.3.0 development; not in any 0.2.x release.
  - **High:** `noxtls_sha1_verify()` returned success when the digest did not match. Present in 0.2.x.
  - **High:** ARIA key setup with an unsupported key type corrupted the stack, and the Camellia one-shot modes read and wrote past caller buffers for invalid lengths.
  - **High:** parsing a malformed PKCS#8 private key could overflow a stack buffer.
  - **High:** a diagnostic global, `noxtls_ecdsa_sign_last_nonce`, kept a copy of every ECDSA signing nonce, from which the private key can be computed. The symbol has been removed: **remove any reference to it.**
  - **High:** a TLS 1.2 server that requires client certificates could be bypassed through session resumption. Such servers **no longer resume sessions**.
  - **High:** TLS 1.2 accepted a Finished message sent outside record protection.
  - **High:** TLS 1.3 and DTLS 1.3 accepted an endpoint's own records when an attacker reflected them back to it. A record that fails authentication is now always rejected with bad_record_mac.
  - **High:** `noxtls_tls13_certificate_verify_build_signed_content()` and its `_ex` variant ignored the caller's buffer size and could write past the buffer. They now return `NOXTLS_RETURN_INVALID_PARAM` and report the required length when the buffer is too small: **check buffer sizes and return codes.**
  - **High:** DTLS 1.3 did not check a record's length field against the received datagram, so any peer could make an endpoint read up to 64 KB past the datagram before authentication.
  - **High:** the TLS 1.3 client could read past its handshake buffer when a short record followed a partly consumed one, before the server was authenticated.
  - **High:** `noxtls_x509_certificate_write_pem()` and `noxtls_x509_csr_create_pem()` ignored `out_max` and could write past the caller's buffer. They now fail without writing when the buffer is too small: **check buffer sizes and return codes.**
  - **High:** a TLS 1.2 server checked RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 client CertificateVerify signatures loosely (no s < n check, and the padding was scanned instead of compared), the same class of flaw as the RSA forgery above.
  - **Medium:** memory leaks that a peer can trigger repeatedly (the TLS 1.3 HelloRetryRequest extension list, and partial TLS 1.2 handshake state at context free), and a leak of every replaced global trust-store snapshot. On a fixed embedded memory pool these exhaust memory.
  - **Medium:** hostname verification matched a SAN DNS name containing a NUL byte by its prefix, and the subject-CN fallback could be spoofed by another subject attribute that contained `CN=`.
  - **Medium:** EC private-key import accepted the scalar 0 and scalars not less than the group order. RSA-PSS verification accepted s + n as well as s, and RSA decryption accepted ciphertexts not less than the modulus.
  - **Low:** a TLS 1.2 CBC padding oracle through the record_overflow error, RSA-PSS ignoring the leftmost bits of the encoded message, and Ed25519 accepting the non-canonical "negative zero" point encoding.

**MISRA API conventions.** Public text parameters and structure fields (hostnames, SNI, ALPN, file paths, passwords, DN and time strings, debug formats) are now `uint8_t` instead of `char`, so cast string literals at call sites. `noxtls_return_t` and most public enums (`noxtls_hash_algos_t`, `noxtls_aes_type_t`, `ecc_curve_t`, `rsa_key_size_t`, the PQC parameter sets and more) are now `uint32_t` typedefs; their numeric values are unchanged. New helpers in `noxtls_ct.h`: bounded `noxtls_copy_u8()`, `noxtls_move_u8()`, and `noxtls_fill_u8()`, plus `noxtls_u8_strlen()`, `noxtls_u8_strcmp()`, and `noxtls_u8_strncmp()`.

**Allocator policy.** Library code allocates only through `NOXTLS_MALLOC`, `NOXTLS_CALLOC`, and `NOXTLS_REALLOC`, and releases through `noxtls_free()`. `scripts/check_allocator_policy.py` (CTest `allocator_policy_check`) rejects raw allocator calls outside the allocator implementation. `noxtls_memory_compat.h` no longer redefines `malloc`/`free`/`calloc`/`realloc`, because MISRA Rule 21.2 forbids redefining standard-library names.

**Host stdio is optional.** Set `NOXTLS_HAVE_FILE_IO=0` (default 1; also available in the ESP-IDF and Zephyr Kconfig) to build without stdio file helpers. File-load APIs then return `NOXTLS_RETURN_FAILED`. `noxtls_debug_printf()` is now a no-op unless you configure CMake with `-DNOXTLS_DEBUG_PRINTF_STDIO=ON`.

SHA-256 HMAC state and ECC inversion scratch are now private per context or per call by default. `NOXTLS_HMAC_SHA256_SHARED_STATE` and `NOXTLS_ECC_SHARED_SCRATCH` (both default OFF) switch to fixed shared storage for externally serialized builds. See [Memory usage](./memory-usage.md#concurrent-crypto-scratch-storage).

**SPAKE2+** (P256-SHA256-HKDF-SHA256-HMAC-SHA256) with two per-context profiles: RFC 9383 (default) and the Matter draft-bar-cfrg-spake2plus-01 key schedule. Added **Matter PASE** helpers for passcode validation, w0/w1 and verifier generation, the PASE context hash, and session-key derivation. Both are off by default (`NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_SPAKE2P`, `NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_SPAKE2P_MATTER`, `NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_MATTER_PASE`). See [SPAKE2+ and Matter PASE](./spake2p.md) and the [SPAKE2+ API](./api/spake2p.md).

**PBKDF2 (RFC 8018)** public API: `noxtls_pbkdf2_hmac()` over HMAC-SHA1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512, with `noxtls_pbkdf2_self_test()` (RFC 6070 vectors). It erases the output on failure. When enabled, X.509 PBES2 private-key decryption uses it. Enable with `NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_PBKDF2` (default OFF). See [Key derivation API](./api/kdf.md).

**AES key wrap (RFC 3394)**: `noxtls_aes_key_wrap()`, `noxtls_aes_key_unwrap()` (constant-time integrity check, output cleared on failure), and `noxtls_aes_keywrap_self_test()`. Built together with AES-ECB. See [AES key wrap](./api/aes_keywrap.md).

**AES-XTS decryption and two-key API.** New `noxtls_aes_xts_encrypt()` and `noxtls_aes_xts_decrypt()` take separate data (Key1) and tweak (Key2) keys, as NIST SP 800-38E requires. New `noxtls_aes_decrypt_xts()` is the inverse of the existing single-key `noxtls_aes_encrypt_xts()`, which uses its one key as both Key1 and Key2. A data unit must be at least 16 bytes. XTS now follows IEEE 1619, so ciphertext written by earlier NoxTLS XTS code is not compatible: see **Behaviour changes and upgrade notes** under Fixed / Resolved below. See [AES XTS](./api/aes_xts.md).

**Bounded PEM writers.** New `noxtls_certificate_der_to_pem_ex()` and `noxtls_csr_der_to_pem_ex()` take the output capacity and return `NOXTLS_RETURN_FAILED` without writing when the PEM text and its NUL terminator do not fit. `noxtls_x509_certificate_write_pem()` and `noxtls_x509_csr_create_pem()` now use them, and `noxtls_x509_certificate_write_pem()` no longer makes a temporary heap copy of the certificate (`NOXTLS_MAX_CERT_SIZE`, 16 to 64 KB). See [Certificates](./api/certs.md).

**Faster P-521.** P-521 field multiplication uses a dedicated reduction modulo the Mersenne prime 2^521 - 1 on the stack instead of generic bignum division, with no heap use and no failure path. Measured with GCC -O2 on a host machine, P-521 ECDSA signing is about 29 times faster (378 ms to 13 ms) and verification about 39 times faster (1,020 ms to 26 ms). Define `NOXTLS_P521_GENERIC_ARITHMETIC=1` to keep the generic path.

**Ed448 is usable.** With `NOXTLS_CFG_FEATURE_ED448` enabled (default OFF), the Ed448 code did not compile, and its arithmetic did not follow RFC 8032. It has been rewritten as a portable C99 implementation that passes the RFC 8032 and OpenSSL test vectors, with the public API unchanged. Field arithmetic and scalar multiplication are constant-time and use no heap; points, reserved bits, and S are decoded strictly; and dom4 is included in every hash, including streaming verification. Measured on an x64 MSVC Release build, signing and verification each take about 4 ms. See [Ed448](./api/ed448.md).

**X.509 explicit verification policy.** `noxtls_x509_verify_cert_with_policy()` verifies a leaf and the intermediates it presents against caller-supplied trust anchors, required Key Usage (all-of), EKU, an optional CRL, and a system or explicit clock, without using the global trust store. It fails closed when the policy has no anchors. `noxtls_x509_certificate_check_validity_at()` checks validity at a caller-supplied time.

**Strict raw X.509 extension lookup** (`noxtls_x509_ext.h`). Iterate extensions or find one by OID with strict DER checks, rejecting duplicate extensions per RFC 5280 section 4.2. `noxtls_x509_oid_is_under_arc()` checks private-enterprise arcs (for example Thread TCAT).

**TLS 1.2 per-context client-certificate policy for servers.** `noxtls_tls12_set_client_verify_policy()` verifies client certificates only against the policy. Session-ID and ticket resumption are declined while a policy is set, so every connection re-authenticates. `noxtls_tls12_get_client_certificate()` returns the accepted client leaf. `noxtls_tls12_context_size()` detects `noxtls_config.h` mismatches between the library and the application.

**Message digests, HMAC, and key derivation:**
  - RIPEMD-160 produced a wrong digest for every input. This was a regression introduced during 0.3.0 development and is not present in 0.2.x releases. Its bit counter is now 64-bit (it previously overflowed at 512 MiB of input).
  - MD4 produced a wrong digest for non-empty messages whose length is a multiple of 64 bytes.
  - BLAKE2s and BLAKE2b produced wrong digests for inputs of one block or more; the implementation now follows RFC 7693, including the full 64-bit BLAKE2b counter.
  - MD5 streaming updates mishandled a buffered partial block and rejected a second short update.
  - All digests now match the reference vectors for both one-shot and chunked input.
  - A failed compression step (for example an accelerator error) could still return success with a wrong digest: SHA-224/256, SHA-384/512, and MD5 let the final padding block's status overwrite an earlier failure, and RIPEMD-160 ignored compression results. Digests now stop at the first failure and erase the output and the context, and the verify helpers never report a match after a hashing error. SHA-3 rejects NULL data with a non-zero length.
  - HMAC with SHA-1, SHA-384, or SHA-512 ignored the status of some inner and outer hash steps and could return success with a wrong MAC. Every status now propagates, and the MAC output, key pads, and hash state are erased on failure. HKDF expand and the PBKDF2 PRF return the underlying error and erase their outputs.

**Symmetric ciphers and AEAD:**
  - ARIA one-shot CBC encryption did not chain the zero-padded final partial block; it now matches AES-CBC. ARIA decryption rejects lengths that are not a multiple of the block size, and CTR and CFB report key-setup errors.
  - ChaCha20-Poly1305 rejects `aad == NULL` with a non-zero `aad_len`, compares the tag in constant time, and erases the computed tag.
  - AES-CCM: removed an undefined shift for the maximum length-field size (L = 8).
  - nRF52: an AES-ECB operation preempted by an interrupt-side AES call could return a wrong block. The ECB transaction now runs with interrupts masked.

**Bignum, DSA, RSA, and Diffie-Hellman:**
  - `noxtls_bn_mod_inv()` returned a wrong value with success for even moduli and when no inverse exists (for example 7^-1 mod 8 returned 2). It now computes correct inverses for odd and even moduli and returns `NOXTLS_RETURN_FAILED` with a zeroed result when the modulus is 1 or less or no inverse exists. The P-256 path is unchanged.
  - `noxtls_dh_generate_key()` could loop forever when the top byte of p was below 0x80. Private values are now drawn by bounded rejection sampling in [2, p - 2], and degenerate p or g values fail cleanly.
  - `noxtls_dh_shared_secret()` used the wrong end of an over-long peer value. A longer peer value is now accepted only when its extra leading bytes are zero.
  - FFDHE ephemeral keys applied the RFC 7919 exponent-length mask to the least significant byte instead of the most significant byte.
  - DH erases DRBG state and private buffers after use and zeroes outputs on failure.
  - `noxtls_bn_mod()` returned success with a zeroed result when an internal allocation failed. Allocation failures now return `NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`, every bignum error propagates with the result zeroed, and modular exponentiation reports memory and reduction errors instead of switching to its fallback path. Hardware bignum hooks fall back to software only on `NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_SUPPORTED` or `NOXTLS_RETURN_FAILED`.
  - DSA key generation, signing, and verification ignored bignum errors. Under memory pressure, signing could return success with an invalid s, and key generation could return x = 1, y = g. Every result is now checked, only r = 0, s = 0, or a non-invertible k is retried, and outputs and secrets are erased on failure.
  - RSA: Miller-Rabin treated a failed exponentiation as "probably prime". Key generation, encryption, CRT decryption, and the blinded private-key operation now check every step and erase outputs on failure.
  - `noxtls_bn_mod_inv()` validates its lengths before writing to the result buffer. It previously zeroed the buffer before rejecting an oversized modulus length.

**ECC, ECDSA, EdDSA, X25519, and X448:**
  - secp224k1: the 225-bit group order was truncated, so no ECDSA signature verified and generated keys were reduced incorrectly. All other curve constants were re-checked against SEC 2 and RFC 5639. Because r and s remain 28 bytes, a secp224k1 signature with s of 2^224 or more (probability about 2^-111) is retried when signing and rejected when verifying.
  - Point multiply-and-add failed when one point was a small multiple of the other (seen on secp256k1 and brainpoolP256r1), and P-256 gave a wrong result when one operand was the point at infinity. ECDSA verification now rejects an identity result.
  - `noxtls_ecdsa_sign()` returned success with r = 0 when its retries ran out. It now fails, zeroes the signature, and erases the nonce and its inverse.
  - nRF54 CRACEN: P-256 results are double-checked with an independent blinding factor, and the portable implementation is used if the two results disagree.
  - Under memory pressure, ECC point operations continued after a failed field operation: secp256k1 point multiplication could return success with a wrong point, and key generation could return the point at infinity as a public key. Field and point operations now return the first failure and zero their output. `noxtls_ecc_point_validate_public()` rejects the point at infinity and coordinates that are not less than p, and key generation redraws a zero private key, validates the public key, and erases both on failure. ECDSA, ECDH, X448, and Ed25519 propagate these errors in the same way.
  - After a single DRBG failure, ECC, ECDSA, X25519, X448, Ed25519, Ed448, and RSA key generation and signing failed for the rest of the process, because the internal generator stayed marked as initialized after its state was erased. A DRBG failure now uninstantiates the generator, and the next call re-instantiates it from entropy.
  - `noxtls_ecc_key_free()` erased a fixed 66 bytes of the private-key buffer even when the key's curve had been detached, overrunning a smaller buffer. It now erases the allocated length recorded in the new `d_size` field.

**X.509 certificates and private keys:**
  - Encrypted PKCS#8 private keys could never be decrypted. Decryption now follows RFC 5958 and PBES2 (RFC 8018): PBKDF2 with the PRF named in the key, optional keyLength, AES-128/192/256-CBC with the IV from the parameters, and a padding check.
  - Ed25519 and Ed448 keys whose first byte was 0x04 (or 0x30) were parsed as EC (or RSA) keys. The key type now follows the algorithm OID, and Ed25519/Ed448 certificate signatures are verified.
  - Authority and Subject Key Identifiers never matched. Issuer lookup now prefers key-identifier matches, falls back to name matching, and always requires a valid signature.
  - SEC1 EC private keys kept no public key and were reported as PKCS#8. They now keep the embedded public key and are reported as SEC1, and a stored public key that does not match the private key is rejected.
  - Certificate generation issued a certificate without its extensions when extension encoding failed. It now fails instead.
  - A malformed BOOLEAN in a certificate extension could move the parser past the end of the extension. A BOOLEAN must now be one byte with the value 0x00 or 0xFF, a malformed critical flag or basicConstraints cA value is rejected with `NOXTLS_RETURN_BAD_DATA`, and every cursor advance is checked against the bytes remaining.
  - PKCS#1 private-key parsing returned success with missing key components after an allocation failure. Certificate, PKCS#1, PKCS#8, SEC1, encrypted PKCS#8, PEM, and file loading now erase and free partial results and return `NOXTLS_RETURN_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`, and the DER parse dispatchers stop trying other formats after an allocation failure.
  - `noxtls_x509_parse_time()` returned success without writing or terminating the output when `output_size` was less than 20. It now returns `NOXTLS_RETURN_INVALID_PARAM` with an empty string and always NUL-terminates its output. This was found by fuzzing.

**TLS 1.2:**
  - The client's signature_algorithms extension carried uninitialized bytes, so servers that require an ECDSA scheme rejected the handshake. This was a regression introduced during 0.3.0 development and is not present in 0.2.x releases.
  - The client could not verify DHE-RSA ServerKeyExchange signatures from servers with standard certificates. One verifier now handles DHE and ECDHE, uses the signature scheme the server actually signed with, and requires that scheme to be one the client offered. The ClientHello now also offers rsa_pkcs1_sha512, ecdsa_secp521r1_sha512, and rsa_pss_rsae_sha256/384/512, which the client already verified.
  - `noxtls_tls10_connect()` and `noxtls_tls11_connect()` rejected the TLS 1.0/1.1 ServerHello they had negotiated. The client now accepts exactly the version it offered.
  - The server rejected every X448 ClientKeyExchange; it now accepts X448 and rejects an all-zero shared secret.
  - The client rejected DHE-RSA AES-CCM suites it had offered; it now accepts exactly the suites it offered.
  - A DHE generator g in its minimal encoding was rejected; g is now checked numerically.
  - Trailing bytes after Certificate or ClientKeyExchange are rejected unless they form the next handshake message, and the RSA CertificateVerify length check (which compared bytes to bits) now works.
  - Zero-length records could not be sent with AEAD cipher suites.
  - `noxtls_tls12_context_free()` now erases the premaster and master secrets, traffic keys, IVs, MAC keys, Finished data, and buffered application plaintext held in the context.
  - With a handshake workspace smaller than the fixed message layouts (for example `NOXTLS_TLS_HANDSHAKE_WORKSPACE_SIZE` = 2048), message builders overran the heap block. They now use a dedicated allocation instead.

**TLS 1.3, DTLS, and the unified connection API:**
  - The TLS 1.3 client could crash after a HelloRetryRequest that selected a group other than X25519.
  - The TLS 1.3 client always sent an X25519 key share. It now offers a share for the first configured (EC)DHE group and, after a HelloRetryRequest, exactly one share for the group the server selected, which must be a group the client offered. The server now rejects a second ClientHello that does not carry exactly one share for the group its HelloRetryRequest selected.
  - Post-handshake messages (NewSessionTicket, KeyUpdate) and alerts are processed from an internal buffer, independent of the size of the buffer passed to the read call. A post-handshake message larger than that buffer previously closed the connection.
  - A TLS 1.3 server could select only the last PSK identity offered; selecting any other identity failed. Any offered identity can now be selected, and the identities and binders are fully validated (one binder of at least 32 bytes per identity).
  - The TLS 1.3 client ignored parse errors in EncryptedExtensions. EncryptedExtensions and ServerHello extensions are now validated: a duplicate extension aborts with illegal_parameter and a malformed list with decode_error.
  - 0-RTT: when early data was offered with a PSK, the server now adds the client's EndOfEarlyData to the handshake transcript instead of failing the handshake.
  - DTLS 1.3 post-handshake messages (KeyUpdate, NewSessionTicket, NewConnectionId, RequestConnectionId) were sent under the handshake keys and parsed with TLS framing, so a KeyUpdate ended the connection. They now use the current application keys and DTLS handshake framing, and are acknowledged with ACK records.
  - DTLS 1.3 connection IDs longer than one byte could not be received. The full negotiated length (up to 255 bytes) is now supported.
  - DTLS: a lost first ClientHello was never retransmitted, because epoch 0, sequence 0 was treated as acknowledged before any ACK arrived.
  - DTLS 1.3: a retransmission timeout while waiting for the encrypted server flight aborted the handshake. The client now retransmits and keeps waiting, and the server answers a retransmitted first ClientHello with its HelloRetryRequest again.
  - DTLS 1.2: zero-length handshake messages such as ServerHelloDone were neither sent nor accepted, so DTLS 1.2 handshakes could not complete. They are now sent and accepted as a single empty fragment (RFC 6347 section 4.2.3).
  - DTLS 1.3 record-number protection used a 16-byte key for every cipher suite, but AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 need a 32-byte key (RFC 9147 section 4.2.3), so the record-number mask was computed with the wrong key and read past the stored key. The key now has the AEAD key length.
  - DTLS 1.3 fatal alerts sent after the handshake were protected with the handshake epoch's record-number key, so peers could not read them. They now use the current epoch's keys. After three KeyUpdates (epoch 6, which shares its 2-bit header value with the handshake epoch), the receiver also chose the handshake key; it now selects the key from the full epoch.
  - DTLS: an allocation failure while reassembling a fragmented handshake message led to a NULL pointer dereference on the next fragment. Reassembly state is now committed only after its buffers are allocated and is reset after each message is delivered, which also fixes reassembly of a following message of the same length. An unfragmented retransmission discards partial state.
  - DTLS 1.3 server: an allocation failure while storing the client's key shares left a non-zero share count with no array, which the server then dereferenced. Key shares are now published only after the allocation succeeds. Lengths are also cleared after failed allocations of pending application data and certificates.
  - Unified API: a client using `noxtls_tls_connection_connect()` with automatic version selection on a non-blocking (caller-polled) transport returned `NOXTLS_RETURN_NEGOTIATED_TLS12` instead of continuing with TLS 1.2. It now downgrades to TLS 1.2 as a blocking client does. A client restricted to TLS 1.3 sends a protocol_version alert when the server selects TLS 1.2.
